footer.odor_model: Odor model: odor predictions on this page come from the graph neural network of this site's odor predictor, trained on data from The Good Scents Company and Leffingwell & Associates (Sanchez-Lengeling et al., 2019, arXiv:1910.10685, CC BY-NC), curated and merged by OpenPOM (Barsainyan et al., 2023); the raw data and odor labels are not redistributed here. The model and its predictions are for non-commercial academic demonstration only.
wf.intro: Five projects form one flavor development workflow:
wf.1.title: Predict a molecule's odor
wf.2.title: Browse the odor space
wf.2.desc: See how thousands of molecules relate on an odor map
wf.3.title: Find ingredients / substitutes
wf.3.desc: Search by target flavor, or find molecules that smell alike
wf.4.title: Improve a formulation
wf.4.desc: Bayesian optimization suggests which flavor compounds to add
home.finder.title: Flavor Ingredient Finder
wf.5.title: Interpret GC-MS results
wf.5.desc: Turn instrument data into key aroma compounds and a flavor profile
home.map.title: Odor Space Map
home.perc.title: Why People Smell Differently
home.hero: I turn flavor-lab problems into tools a colleague can use.
home.gcms.one: From a GC-MS peak table to key aroma compounds and OAV/ROAV, across instrument formats.
home.finder.one: Find molecules for a flavor brief, or substitutes that smell alike but differ in structure.
home.odor.one: A graph neural network that predicts odor descriptors from molecular structure.
home.fi.one: Bayesian optimization for dairy flavor, and a comparison of your own sample with a target.
home.map.one: 5,000+ molecules laid out by predicted odor, compared with a layout by structure.
home.taste.one: Predicts whether a small molecule is sweet, bitter, umami or tasteless.
home.perc.one: How much of the difference in smell ratings comes from the molecule, personal taste or noise.
home.kb.one: Key odorants and detected compounds, searchable by food or compound.
